verses.text: The Pharisees and some legal teachers who had come from Jerusalem gathered around Jesus.
They saw some of his disciples eating with hands they considered unclean—that is, hands that hadn’t been washed—and they called it out.
The Pharisees, and Jews generally, wouldn’t eat without washing their hands and forearms, holding tight to the tradition handed down by the elders.
When they came back from the marketplace, they wouldn’t eat without first washing. They followed many other traditions too: washing cups, pitchers, bronze dishes, and dining couches.
So the Pharisees and legal teachers asked Jesus, “Why don’t your disciples follow the elders’ tradition? They’re eating with unwashed hands!”
Jesus answered, “Isaiah called it right when he prophesied about you hypocrites: ‘These people honor me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me.
“‘Their worship is empty, because they teach human rules as if they were God’s commands.’
“You let go of God’s command and hold tight to human tradition—washing pitchers and cups. And that’s just one example of the many things you do.”
He continued, “You’re good at setting aside God’s command so you can keep your own tradition.
“Moses said, ‘Honor your father and mother,’ and, ‘Whoever speaks evil against father or mother must be put to death.’
“But you say, ‘If someone tells their father or mother, “Anything I could have used to help you is Corban”—that is, dedicated to God—’
“then you no longer let them do anything to help their father or mother.
“In this way you cancel God’s word through the tradition you’ve handed down. And you do plenty of things like that.”
Jesus called the whole crowd over and said, “All of you, listen and understand this.
“Nothing outside a person can make them unclean by going into them. What comes out of a person is what makes them unclean.
“If you have ears to hear, listen!”
When Jesus went into a house away from the crowd, his disciples asked him what the parable meant.
He said, “Are you still missing it too? Don’t you see that nothing entering a person from outside can make them unclean,
“because it doesn’t go into their heart; it goes into their stomach, then out into the latrine?” In saying this, he declared all foods clean.
He went on: “What comes out of a person is what makes them unclean.
“Evil thoughts come from within, from people’s hearts: sexual immorality, stealing, murder, adultery,
“greed, wickedness, deceit, shameless desire, envy, slander, arrogance, and foolishness.
“All these evil things come from within and make a person unclean.”
Jesus left that place and went to the region of Tyre and Sidon. He entered a house, hoping nobody would know he was there, but he couldn’t stay hidden.
A woman whose little daughter had an unclean spirit heard about Jesus. She came in and fell at his feet.
The woman was Greek, a Syrophoenician by birth. She begged Jesus to drive the demon out of her daughter.
Jesus told her, “Let the children eat first. It isn’t right to take the children’s bread and throw it to the dogs.”
She answered, “Yes, Lord. But even the dogs under the table get to eat the children’s crumbs.”
Jesus told her, “Because of what you said, go home. The demon has left your daughter.”
She went home and found her child lying on the bed, with the demon gone.
Jesus left the region of Tyre, traveled through Sidon, and came to the Sea of Galilee through the middle of the Decapolis region.
People brought him a man who was deaf and could hardly speak. They begged Jesus to lay his hand on him.
Jesus took the man away from the crowd to a private spot. He put his fingers in the man’s ears, then spat and touched his tongue.
Jesus looked up to heaven, sighed, and said to him, “Ephphatha!”—that means, “Be opened!”
Right away, the man’s ears opened, his tongue was freed, and he spoke clearly.
Jesus ordered them not to tell anyone. But the more he told them to keep quiet, the more widely they spread the news.
The people were amazed beyond words. They said, “He’s done everything well! He even makes deaf people hear and people who can’t speak talk!”
